item.title: French Government Calls Emergency Meetings With Platforms Over Protests
item.description: TikTok and other sites were told to curb protest footage and AI-altered images, while online retailers like Vinted and eBay reportedly signed an agreement stop looted goods from flooding resale sites.

item.title: An AI Agent Joined a Listserv of Top Internet Researchers. The Reply-All Chaos Is Still Unfolding
item.description: Hysteria over the agent's appearance in a 7,500-person group reveals that internet experts have outdated notions of privacy.

item.title: OpenAI Engineer Accused of Spying on Executives Ordered to Remain in Custody
item.description: A judge ordered Abdulrahman Alfozan to remain in custody, likening the Saudi government’s offer to secure the former OpenAI engineer’s release to a “blank check.”

item.title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
item.description: Around 80 pages on WhatsApp’s website exposed instructions that were designed for its chatbot, including “WHAT NOT TO SAY.” Meta says a bug caused the issue.

item.title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
item.description: The entertainment giant hopes to get trust and safety tech, among other IP, from a startup whose chatbots dozens of states allege encouraged minors to self-harm and kill their parents.

item.title: OnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk Dirty
item.description: Adult performers are questioning why Meta allows its AI agent to sext while restricting their social media accounts.

item.title: Data Centers Have a New PR Plan: Your Kid’s Field Trip
item.description: Amid a wave of backlash, some industry-friendly groups are employing creative and time-tested strategies to woo the youth.

item.title: Why AI Isn’t Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
item.description: The DNA inside our cells isn’t just a series of instructions, but something far more dynamic. Like scientists, AI models don't yet have the data to properly decode it.

item.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
item.description: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there.

item.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’
item.description: MIT professor Sherry Turkle warns that people have become dangerously enmeshed with chatbots.
